nonStandardRelationType.description: A relationship that doesn't cleanly fit the seven standard PRD S10.2 relation types, recorded as "other" with a required relationTypeNote explaining the resolution, per spec.md Edge Cases and research.md's decision.
nonStandardRelationType.resolvedAs: relationType: "other", with relationTypeNote explaining that Heap Sort instantiates the Priority Queue interface's generic sort pattern rather than being explained-by, contained-in, contrasted-with, generalized-from, or exemplifying it -- none of the seven standard types fit "produces a concrete instance of".

multiAliasConcept.description: A concept appearing under two different names in different source artifacts, represented as one canonical concept with recorded aliases rather than two separate concepts, per spec.md Edge Cases.
multiAliasConcept.evidence: lecture-09-breadth-first-search's own title spells out "Breadth-First Search", while lecture-10-depth-first-search's "Previously" section refers back to it only as "Breadth-First Search (BFS)" -- both terms are real, source-grounded, and refer to the identical algorithm across two different lecture artifacts.

multiTargetEvidence.description: A hypothetical (illustrative, not a real logged student interaction) piece of evidence that plausibly supports more than one concept and more than one relationship at once, demonstrating the EvidenceEvent schema's conceptIds[]/edgeIds[] arrays are exercised together, per spec.md Edge Cases and PRD S10.3.
multiTargetEvidence.note: A single answer explaining why BFS requires a graph as input AND why level sets are what make BFS work is evidence about two concepts and two edges simultaneously -- exactly the case the schema's array-valued conceptIds/edgeIds fields exist to support, per data-model.md.

ambiguousQuestion.description: A deliberately ambiguous question, included so the question-ambiguity evaluation rubric (spec User Story 3) has a real positive test case rather than only clean examples, per spec.md Edge Cases.
ambiguousQuestion.whyAmbiguous: "Closer to" a max-heap or min-heap is not a metric defined anywhere in the course material (Lecture 8 only defines the Max-Heap Property as a strict per-node boolean condition), so the question has no single correct answer as phrased.
